# Smart glasses designed to assist with navigation. — devlog

> This work presents the development of a low-cost smart glasses system designed to assist with spatial navigation and accident prevention. The prototype utilizes an ESP32-S3 microcontroller to manage a transparent OLED display, which functions as a Head-Up Display (HUD) by projecting directional arrows and status icons directly into the user's field of view without obstructing the surroundings. The system operates in conjunction with a web application (React) running on a smartphone, which handles GPS route processing and transmits simplified commands to the device via Bluetooth. For active safety, the hardware incorporates a VL53L0X laser sensor for the immediate detection of physical obstacles.

## Build

### 2026-09-30 — First, I focused on setting up the schematics for the glasses. The system uses an ESP32-S3 microcontroller as the project's "brain." I positioned the 1.51-inch transparent OLED display on the right le

**1.5h**

First, I focused on setting up the schematics for the glasses. The system uses an ESP32-S3 microcontroller as the project's "brain." I positioned the 1.51-inch transparent OLED display on the right lens to act as a Head-Up Display (HUD), projecting information directly into the field of view without obstructing the view of the surroundings. For safety, I installed a VL53L0X laser distance sensor on the right temple to detect obstacles ahead. Power is managed by a 3.7V Li-Po battery integrated with a TP4056 charging module..

### 2026-09-30 — I worked on programming the ESP32-S3 using the Arduino IDE. I implemented the I2C communication bus, simultaneously connecting the OLED Display and the laser sensor. I configured the U8g2lib library f

**2h**

I worked on programming the ESP32-S3 using the Arduino IDE. I implemented the I2C communication bus, simultaneously connecting the OLED Display and the laser sensor. I configured the U8g2lib library for the graphical interface on the display and adjusted the logic for the active buzzer, ensuring it emits an immediate sound alert if the sensor detects a very close object (risk of collision). I also set up the Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) server infrastructure to receive external commands.
